title: Domain adaptation and fine-tuning for domain-specific LLMs: Abi Aryan
talk_summary: A survey talk on domain adaptation and fine-tuning methods (adapters, prefix tuning, LoRA/QLoRA) plus data hygiene and evaluation advice for domain-specific LLMs.

takeaways.technique: Multi-component evaluation instead of single metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Evaluate models across four lenses: metric-based (BLEU/ROUGE), tool-based (auto-evaluators that catch compilation errors), model-based (smaller model judging another), and human-in-the-loop, rather than relying on loss/perplexity alone.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to be looking at evaluation from four different perspectives or four different components

takeaways.technique: Tool-based auto-evaluation for fast error catching
takeaways.what_they_do: Use auto-evaluator libraries that run generated output through tools to catch compilation/runtime errors quickly rather than judging text similarity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that is able to catch the compilation errors very quickly

takeaways.what_they_do: Load few-shot examples dynamically at inference time to handle data/prompt drift and manage cost, instead of baking examples into a fixed prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using in context learning with Dynamic example loading allows you to be able to deal with that particular problem while also making sure that you are able to do uh cost management

takeaways.what_they_do: Break a broad task into narrow specific subtasks rather than training/prompting one model for the whole domain.
takeaways.evidence_quote: breaking down this task into smaller task

takeaways.what_they_do: Remove duplicate entries from training data because duplication causes memorization and bias toward repeated examples.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the memorization which happens in models is mainly because of dat duplication
